# requires: logging
#
# One property lets several processes on several machines append to one file:
# a whole record goes out in one write, so writers interleave whole lines rather
# than halves of two. A record too big for that cap has three possible fates and
# only one of them keeps the property and the evidence.
#
# `over` counts lines longer than the cap, `marked` counts lines carrying the
# shrink mark, and `torn` counts lines carrying a split character. The exact
# length of a shrunk line is not asserted, and must not be: two implementations
# shrinking by different amounts both keep the rule, and pinning the number
# would make one of them wrong for no reason.
machine file
auto A
cap A 512
record R 0
msg R 8000
write A R
held A
record S 0
write A S
held A

# The message is not the only thing that can be too long. A record whose
# retained metadata alone exceeds the cap is the case with no answer if
# shrinking only ever shortens the message: a one-character message cannot get
# shorter by halving, and an empty one cannot get shorter at all.
record T 0
job T 1024
msg T 1
write A T
held A
msg T 0
write A T
held A

# `wide` makes the message out of two-byte characters, so a shrink that slices by
# byte index has somewhere to cut one in half. 511 of them is 1022 bytes, and
# every halving of 1022 is an odd byte index -- 511, 255, 127 and so on down --
# so an implementation that halves by bytes splits a character on any machine,
# whatever its framing costs. A line is UTF-8 or it is not the format this layer
# claims to write.
machine file
auto B
cap B 200
record W 0
msg W 511 wide
write B W
held B

# A cap below the smallest record this layer can encode is refused, and the file
# stays empty. Writing anyway would break the interleaving property for every
# other writer sharing the file.
machine file
auto C
cap C 32
write C S
held C

# expect 6: ok where=file [LOG-S6]
# expect 7: ok lines=1 over=0 marked=1 torn=0 [LOG-S6]
# expect 9: ok where=file
# expect 10: ok lines=2 over=0 marked=1 torn=0 [LOG-S6]
# expect 14: ok where=file [LOG-S9]
# expect 15: ok lines=3 over=0 marked=2 torn=0 [LOG-S9]
# expect 17: ok where=file [LOG-S9]
# expect 18: ok lines=4 over=0 marked=3 torn=0 [LOG-S9]
# expect 24: ok where=file [LOG-R8]
# expect 25: ok lines=1 over=0 marked=1 torn=0 [LOG-R8]
# expect 29: refused [LOG-S10]
# expect 30: ok lines=0 over=0 marked=0 torn=0 [LOG-S10]
